In between

M5 · Ask the turn

B3's numbered pins and slot, plus one line under the slot where you type to the turn. ✦ Ask answers a question about what happened, with #n citations you can open, reply to or re-rank in place. ⌁ Tell takes a plain-words note about what matters and turns it into one previewed change: a mark, a weight or a category. Replies are inline tokens in today's composer.

Builds on
B3, through M3's build of it: the pins, clustering, loupe, slot, pager, keys, the axis line (Ask chip, unread chip, levels), the ✦ recap pin and the ±1 importance slider are all kept. What's new:
  • An ask line at the foot of the slot, with two modes: ✦ Ask and ⌁ Tell.
  • A third slot view, Answer, beside Message and Recap.
  • Citations in the recap and in answers open a small card instead of jumping.
  • M3's composer lanes are gone. Replies are inline .ref tokens in today's composer.
Placement
Everything stays in the activity card. The ask line sits under the slot, above the card's bottom edge, so it reads as "ask about this turn" rather than "message the agent". Answers and proposals replace the slot's contents, with the question in italics where the timestamp usually is. The composer below the card is unchanged apart from reply tokens.
Live
The slot is on the Ask #24, which you're answering. The draft in the composer holds ? #24 and ◆ #18 tokens with text around them. Both pins wear ✎. The ask line offers live questions: "What is it doing now?", "Anything risky since 27:15?", "What should I review first?". Answers use only what's surfaced plus the log so far, and say so.
Settled
The mockup shows a question already asked: "What happened to the legacy path?". The answer cites #6, #33, #31 and #34 and says what nothing in the turn covers (the flag-on path is untested). "Clear" returns to the recap, which is where a settled turn with unread messages opens.
Recap
  • Opening it: ✦ at the right end of the lane, as in M3. Its badge counts the unread messages it covers.
  • Asking beyond it: the recap is the default answer. The ask line is for the question it didn't answer. Settled suggestions are "What happened to the legacy path?", "Why isn't phone-sidebar recaptured?" and "What should I review first?".
  • Citations: #24 opens a card with the message's type, time, level and first three lines, plus Open, ↩ Reply, ▲ and ▼. Open puts it in the slot with a "‹ ✦ Recap" or "‹ ✦ Answer" pill back.
  • Settings: Recap sets model, when, scope and length, and can turn Ask off.
Read-state
As in M3.
  • What marks a message read: moving the slot off it, or "Mark 13 read" under the recap. Reading a recap or an answer marks nothing, and neither does opening a citation card.
  • How unread shows: a dot on the pin, a "● Unread" pill in the slot and "● 9 unread" on the axis.
  • Next unread: the axis chip or n.
Importance-feedback
  • Direct: the ±1 slider in the slot, or ▲/▼ on any citation card, without leaving the answer. Each writes one line to feedback.jsonl.
  • In words: ⌁ Tell with "#26 matters more" proposes a one-level raise for #26, with your words as the reason. Accept applies it and the pin gains ▲.
  • Category-level: "Milestones are noise" proposes Milestone 40 → 30 and shows what it changes in this turn (nothing: #34 and #21 were already All). Accept writes categories.json and Settings updates.
  • Nothing silent: every Tell ends in a card with Accept or Dismiss. Tell never edits without it.
Reply-to
  • Replying: ↩ Reply in the slot, ↩ Reply on a citation card, or r drops a ? #24 Ask token at the caret in the composer. You type around it.
  • Already in the draft: the button reads "✎ In draft" and puts the caret after the existing token instead of adding a second one.
  • Removing: × on the token.
  • Sending: today's Send. The tokens compile to Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): "…" blocks.
Categories
Settings › Categories, with ⌁ Tell at the top.
  • Tell: "Flaky or skipped tests are their own thing" proposes ≈ Flaky at weight 50 with a definition, and explains where 50 sits (Balanced, never Key). Accept adds the row, highlighted, with "⌁ from …" underneath so you can see where it came from.
  • When it already exists: "treat perf numbers as their own thing" answers that ⚡ Perf (70) already covers it, from your note on Sep 19, and changes nothing. The Perf row carries that provenance.
  • Retiring: "Stop surfacing corrections" proposes retiring ↶ Correction and lists this turn's Corrections that would fold. Ask can't be retired.
  • Manual: the conventional list is still there, with −/+ by 5, ↺ reset, Edit, Retire or Delete, and "+ Add category".
Collapsible
▾ folds the slot to a one-line peek and hides the ask line with it, so a folded card is 5 lines on desktop. Final hides pins, slot and ask line. Answers are one slot view, never stacked.
Short-session-threads
A settled turn with the recap open is about 13 lines on desktop (head 1, pins and strip 2, axis 1, slot 6, ask line 2) and about 17 on the phone. Folded, 5 and 6. Answers are not saved to the thread, so asking adds nothing to history.
Easy-to-read
One message, recap or answer at a time at 13.5px. Answers are short paragraphs or a numbered list, and they cite rather than quote, so the card stays small. The citation card shows three lines of the source without moving the slot off the answer.
Mobile-friendly
  • Pins: 24px, and the whole strip is a tap target with the loupe on drag.
  • Ask line: 32px mode buttons ("✦ Ask" and "⌁ Tell"), field and send. Suggestions scroll sideways on one row.
  • Citation card: 30px actions, clamped to the slot width.
  • Cost: the ask line adds about 70px to the card, which the phone feels most.
Consistency
Identical on both: pins, ✦, axis, slot, slider, ask line, answers, citation cards, reply tokens and the Tell box. Divergences:
  • The phone labels the mode "⌁ Tell" instead of "⌁ Tell conduit what matters", and hides the slot's type label in answer view.
  • Suggestions wrap on desktop and scroll on the phone.
  • The pager moves to the slot footer on the phone.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
  • #7: 7 ↵, switching to All if needed. On the phone, drag the loupe.
  • The Ask: a or the "? #24" chip.
  • Next unread: n.
  • New: / focuses the ask line. "Where did it decide the flag?" is often faster than scrubbing, and the answer's citation is one click from the message.
At-150
  • Pins: group pills, as in B3.
  • Ask: scales best of anything here. A question costs the same at 150 messages as at 30, and answers still cite a handful.
  • Recap: still scoped to unread.
  • Tell: unaffected by message count.
Build-cost
L. It needs:
  • Per-message read state in the event store.
  • A feedback.jsonl writer that also records Tell notes.
  • Daemon-side recap and ask calls (one sonnet-5 call each, over surfaced messages plus the log).
  • A Tell call that returns one structured change (mark, weight, add, retire, or none) against categories.json, plus the preview of its effect on the open turn.
  • Inline reply tokens in the composer, which are cheaper than M3's lanes.
Trade-off
  • Height: the ask line costs two lines on every expanded card, even when you never ask.
  • Parsing: Tell reads natural language, so it can misread. Every Tell ends in a proposal you accept, and it falls back to "I couldn't turn that into a change" with examples, but a wrong-but-plausible proposal is still possible.
  • Trust: answers can be wrong about the turn. They cite every claim so you can check, and they say when nothing covers the question.
  • Two ways in: importance can be changed three ways (slider, card, Tell), which is more to learn than M3.

In between

M6 · Weighted lane

The pin lane becomes a bar lane: each surfaced message is a bar as tall as its prominence, standing against the Key 70 and Balanced 40 lines, so you drag a bar to re-rank one message and drag a category's column to watch all of its bars cross the lines.

Builds on
B3. The numbered pin lane becomes a bar lane on the same time axis: a bar per surfaced message, its height the prominence (weight × Jev p), against two horizontal lines, Key 70 and Balanced 40. Numbers ride on top of every bar at or above the chosen level. B3's slot, pager, caret, fold, level control and number-jump stay. B3's clustering goes: bars are 5px wide, so 34 fit without merging. The loupe survives, but only on the phone.
Placement
All inside the one activity card: head (with "9 unread ⇥"), bar lane, unread dots under the baseline, the duration strip, an axis row (level, ⚖ Weights, ✦ Recap, ? #24), then the slot. The final reply follows the card, and the composer sits under it as usual.
Live
New bars rise at the right edge, and the slot follows the newest (#30) until you pick another. The "9 unread" pill steps through the unread bars. The level lines show what Balanced would hide: bars below the lit line are drawn at a quarter opacity rather than removed, so you see what's being filtered.
Settled
The slot opens on the recap, "Since you last read" (13 updates). #1 carries a hatched cap from its own 37 up past the Balanced line, labelled "1▲": that's the "▲ you" mark, visible without a tap. The step log opens from the head.
Recap
Conventional. ✦ Recap on the axis turns the slot into the recap, with a scope switch (Since you last read, Whole turn; Live offers only the first). Each [#n] chip selects that bar and shows the message, and "‹ Recap" goes back. Footer: model, count, time, cost. Settings › Recap sets the model (sonnet-5 by default), when, scope and length.
Read-state
A message you open in the slot becomes read after 1.5s. "Mark unread" or m toggles it back, and the recap's "Mark 13 read" clears the lot. Unread shows as a white dot under the bar, a "● unread" chip in the slot, and the count in the head pill and figure caption, which update together.
Importance-feedback
Drag a bar up or down. It follows your pointer, clamped to one level, and on release it snaps to the next level: a hatched cap shows how far you lifted it above Jev's height, and a dashed ghost shows how far you pushed it down. ▲ More / ▼ Less in the slot, or ↑/↓ on the focused lane, do the same. A toast confirms "▲ #26 All → Balanced · appended to feedback.jsonl · Undo". Each mark writes one JSON line (msg, text, Jev's type and p, mark, reason). A mark never changes a weight.
Reply-to
↩ Reply (or r) drops a .ref token at the composer's caret, or at the end if the caret was never placed. Click another bar, Reply again, type between them. × or Backspace removes one. The desktop "Preview" shows exactly what the agent gets: a "Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): …" quote block before each typed answer.
Categories
Weights are columns. Each column shows its weight as a bar, with this turn's messages of that type as dots at weight × p, plotted against the 70 and 40 lines. Drag a column and the dots, and the lane's bars, cross the lines live, and the level counts update. It works in the card (⚖ Weights) and in Settings › Surfacing, where the rows add Retire/Restore and Reset for built-ins, Edit/Delete for customs (⚡ Perf), and "+ New category". Reweighting is free because p is stored. A new category needs Jev to rerun, so it offers a $0.02 dry run on this turn.
Collapsible
▾ folds the slot to a one-line peek. The lane stays, because it is the activity strip. Final (level control) removes the bars and the slot, leaving today's plain strip and "Final only · 34 hidden · Show". Older turns open folded.
Short-session-threads
Desktop: head, lane (about 4 lines tall with labels), strip and axis come to about 7 lines, and the slot about 5 more, so 12 in all, or 8 folded. Phone: about 16, or 10 folded. The lane is 2 lines taller than B3's pin lane. That's the cost of the height channel. It's all one activity card.
Easy-to-read
What matters is literally taller, and the lines say why it's shown. The slot reads at 13.5px, full text, with the arithmetic beside the actions ("p .83 × 40 = 33 → All") so no rank is a mystery. The weak spot is the numbers: at 10px on bar tops, some low bars lose their label to a neighbour. The slot and a hover title fill in.
Mobile-friendly
Bars shrink to 3px, which no finger can grab, so a touch on the lane opens a ×5 loupe above it. In the loupe the bars are 9px wide and every one is numbered. Drag sideways to scrub, and drag a bar vertically to re-rank it there. The slot's actions are four 32px buttons with labels. The composer keeps its full width, with tokens at 12px.
Consistency
Identical on both: the bar lane, lines, labels, unread dots, slot actions, recap-in-slot, toast, and the weight columns in settings. Divergence: the phone re-ranks inside the loupe rather than on the lane (a 3px bar can't be dragged), and it drops the Preview toggle and the in-card ⚖ Weights, leaving weights to settings. The phone's pager moves into a footer row with the arithmetic.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
#7: type 7 on the focused lane (or click its bar, dim at Balanced but still clickable). The Ask: a, or the ? #24 chip, one click. Its glowing bar is the tallest, so it's also easy to aim at. Next unread: u or the "9 unread ⇥" pill, one click each. Phone: the ? #24 and unread pills, one tap each. #7 takes a loupe touch and a tap.
At-150
At 150, 5px bars overlap on desktop (around 3.5px per message over 530px), so desktop also uses the loupe for any stretch denser than 6px per bar. The height channel still reads at a glance: the tall spikes are the Asks and blockers. Labels shrink to Key and Balanced only. The unread count, recap citations and reply tokens are unchanged: numbers are stable, and cites select the bar and open the loupe on it.
Build-cost
M. It needs B3's timestamps plus p stored per message (already there for levels), a canvas-or-DOM bar lane, vertical-drag handling, the loupe, and the weights editor wired to the lane. Storage: feedback.jsonl appends and categories.json. The recap needs one model call per request.
Trade-off
It's the most honest picture of why something surfaced. The cost: it's a chart in the transcript. Two extra lines per turn, bar labels that fight at density, and a gesture (vertical drag) that has to be discovered, though ▲/▼ sit beside it. The in-card weights editor is powerful, and also easy to misread as "just this turn": the toast says "all sessions".

In between

M7 · Review mode

The turn stays one compact M2 strip. Catching up is a separate, deliberate mode: "Review 13 ▸" opens a focused reader with the recap and its citations beside the message card, triage keys, a read-progress bar, and a reply tray that drops into the composer when you leave.

Builds on
M2. It keeps the scrub strip (pins in two rows above the duration strip, a thumb, the Ask chip, levels) and its pop-up card, which gains ▲ ▼ ↩ ○. New here is a separate review mode: the catch-up happens in a reader you open, not in the transcript.
Placement
Transcript: one activity card holding the head (with "Review N ▸"), the strip, and a card above it when a pin is picked. Review on desktop is a two-pane panel docked under the final reply, standing in for the composer while open (the composer and its draft come back on exit). On phone it's a full-screen pager over the session.
Live
The strip grows and the card follows the newest (#30) until you pick a pin. "Review 9 ▸" counts the unread. Review works mid-turn: its queue is fixed when you open it, and new arrivals join at the end, so nothing reshuffles under you.
Settled
Review opens on "Since you last read": 13 in the queue, the recap on the left, #22 on the right. The strip above still shows #1 labelled "1▲" (your mark), and the Whole-turn queue lists #1 with its ▲. The final reply sits above the panel, unobstructed.
Recap
The recap is the first thing in review: the left pane on desktop, page 0 on phone. Scope switch: Since you last read, Whole turn. Each [#n] opens that message in the card pane (desktop) or jumps to its page (phone), and the cite for the open message stays highlighted, so the recap works as a table of contents. Footer: model, count, time, cost.
Read-state
Review is where reading happens, so progress is explicit: a bar and "4 / 13 read" in the review header. Moving past a card (j, e, ›, a swipe) marks it read. u or "○ Mark unread" undoes that. The transcript's pins carry a white unread dot, and the Review button and captions show the live count. A pin opened in the transcript card becomes read after 1.5s.
Importance-feedback
▲ More / ▼ Less on every card, in both the transcript and review (+ / − in review). A mark moves the message one level and writes a line to feedback.jsonl, and the toast has Undo. The card shows "Balanced · ▲ you → Key". A mark never changes a category weight.
Reply-to
In the transcript card, ↩ Reply drops a .ref at the composer's caret, the same as everywhere. In review, ↩ Reply (r) adds the message to a reply tray with a one-line field for your answer, so you can reply to five things without leaving. "Done · drop 2 replies into composer" (or Esc) exits and inserts each token and its text at the caret, ready to edit before sending. Nothing is sent automatically.
Categories
Conventional: Settings › Surfacing › Categories is a list with a detail pane. Selecting a category shows its weight slider, ticked at the Key 70 and Balanced 40 thresholds, with its effect on this turn ("1 of 12 Findings clear Balanced. Balanced shows 16 in all", updating as you drag), its definition, and Retire, or Restore once retired. The custom ⚡ Perf adds Edit and Delete. "+ New category" gives glyph, name, colour, definition and weight, and a $0.02 dry run on this turn. On phone the list pushes to the detail.
Collapsible
The card closes by tapping the pin again or with Esc, leaving just the strip (M2's compact form). Final (level) hides the pins and shows today's plain strip. Review mode is itself the "expanded" state and closes with Esc.
Short-session-threads
The shortest of mine. Closed, the turn is the head, two pin rows, the strip and the axis: about 5 lines on desktop, 6 on phone, with the card adding about 5 when open. Review adds nothing to the thread's length on phone (it's an overlay). On desktop it replaces the composer while you're in it.
Easy-to-read
Review reads like an inbox: one message at 13px (14.5px on phone), full text, its type and time, the recap beside it as context, and a queue with unread bold, read grey. The transcript card clamps nothing. What it gives up is the in-place scan: to read three messages without review you still scrub pins one at a time.
Mobile-friendly
The pager suits a phone well: one message per screen, swipe or ‹ › (36px), a 2×2 grid of 38px actions, reply fields inline under the card, and a sticky "Done ▸" with the tray count. The strip and card in the transcript use M2's phone sizes (12px pins, 32px card actions).
Consistency
The same model on both: a strip in the thread, review as a mode with recap first, the same card actions, the tray, and Done drops into the composer. The difference is form: two panes on desktop, pages on phone (the recap is page 0 rather than a side pane). Triage keys are desktop-only.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
#7: scrub to its pin, or in review switch to Whole turn and click its queue row. Two clicks, no typing. The Ask: the "? #24" chip on the strip, one click, and in review it's the first cite in the recap. Next unread: "Review ▸" then j / e, the fastest triage of the set once you're in. Phone: Review, then swipe. #7 on phone takes a scrub.
At-150
The strip is M2's, so at 150 the pins merge into dots and the card is the only way to read one. Review is what scales: a queue of 40 unread scrolls, triage keys stay one keystroke per message, and the recap cites become the way in. The tray and progress are unchanged. #n stays stable in cites, tokens and queue rows.
Build-cost
M. M2's strip plus a review panel and pager: queue state, a keyboard map, the tray (a local draft store per session, so the tray survives a reload), and one recap call per open. No new storage beyond feedback.jsonl and categories.json.
Trade-off
It separates reading from watching: you're never forced to triage in the transcript, and when you do triage it's fast and keyboard-first. The cost is a mode. Things you'd glance at get hidden behind a click, and the tray is a second draft place, which can surprise you ("where did my reply go?"). The Done label names the count to soften that. On desktop the panel displacing the composer is a real cost while the agent is live, so Live keeps the draft untouched.

Off the wall

Deliberately unusual. Some are unshippable as they stand, but each hides an idea worth stealing.

Off the wall

W1 · Newspaper edition

The turn stays one compact block with a Stop Press ticker. The recap is printed as a front page: a masthead, a headline, the recap as the lede, and desk columns in which every story is a cited message. You rank a story by dragging it above or below the fold, and read ones go grey like visited links.

Builds on
M2, compressed further. The turn keeps one strip with a tick per surfaced message (a white dot while unread). M2's pop-up card becomes a one-line Stop Press ticker with ‹ › ▲ ▼ ✉ ○. The new part is the edition, an opened mode that renders the recap and the surfaced messages as a front page.
Placement
Transcript: one activity card (head, strip, ticker, and an "Extra!" line that opens the edition). The edition unfolds as a sheet under the final reply and above the composer (on phone, at the end of the thread), then folds back to the Extra! line. Stories carry their own actions, so the composer is never covered.
Live
Stop Press shows the newest story (#30), and ‹ › steps through the others. "Extra! 9 unread since 27:15" opens a Late edition marked "still printing", which uses the live recap. The Full edition is disabled until the turn ends, because a front page for a running turn would re-lay itself out under you.
Settled
The Late edition, 44:30, is open. The masthead reads "The Typed Session List". The headline is "One question waits on you as the deep link ships". The lede is the since-you-last-read recap. The lead is #24 ("Waiting on you"), followed by the Decisions and Milestones desks, the fold, and "In brief". "Full" swaps to the whole-turn edition, where #1 sits on the Findings desk above the fold with "▲ you" in its kicker.
Recap
The recap is the lede, with a drop cap and a byline for model, count, time and cost. Every [#n] cites a story on the same page: clicking one scrolls to that story, flashes it and marks it read. Late means since you last read; Full means the whole turn. Settings › Editorial sets the writer model, the print run (when), the edition (scope), the length and the cost.
Read-state
Unread headlines are bold. Read ones turn grey and light, like visited links, so the page itself shows what's left. Opening a headline, following a cite, or stepping the ticker past a story marks it read. ○ marks it unread again. The count lives on the Extra! line and the captions. The strip ticks carry a white dot while unread.
Importance-feedback
Drag a story across the page: onto the lead (Key), above the fold (Balanced), into In brief (All), or onto Spiked (the log). ▲/▼ do the same one step at a time, and are the only way on touch. Each move re-lays the page, adds "▲ you" to the kicker, and appends a line to feedback.jsonl, with Undo in a toast. Section weights are never changed by a move; the ledger feeds the "Ask an agent to tune" flow.
Reply-to
✉ "Letter to the editor" on a story or the ticker clips a .ref to the composer caret, so several go in with your text between them. × or Backspace removes one. The agent receives the kit serialisation: Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): "…" blocks in place of each token.
Categories
Settings › Sections: each category is a newspaper section on a desk, and its weight is shown as column inches (weight ÷ 10). A story runs to inches × Jev's p: 4 in makes the front page, 7 in leads. Use − and + (0.5 in steps) or drag the ruler. Retiring a built-in moves it to Discontinued with Restore. "+ Launch a section" takes glyph, colour, name, desk, definition and inches, with a dry run. ⚡ Perf and any new section get Edit and Fold (delete).
Collapsible
"Fold ▴" closes the edition back to the Extra! line. The ticker can't be hidden, but it's one line. In brief items are one line until you open one. Spiked is a closed <details>.
Short-session-threads
Folded, a settled turn is 4 lines on desktop (head, strip, ticker, Extra!). On phone it's 6 (the ticker actions take a row) or the 5-line masthead teaser. The edition is a mode, not part of the thread.
Easy-to-read
This is where the design is strongest: serif headlines, desks, and a lead that is obviously the thing to answer. Read ones grey out, so you scan for the black. The weakness is that headlines are cut automatically at the first sentence break, so some read awkwardly (#6 is one long sentence), and a real build would need the recap model to write them.
Mobile-friendly
One column, with 32px action grids on each story and a 38px segmented toggle. HTML5 drag-and-drop doesn't work on touch, so on phone the fold is reached with ▲/▼ only, which loses the signature gesture. The edition is long on phone: about 3 screens for the Late edition.
Consistency
The masthead, zones, story anatomy, actions and toasts are identical on both. Only the layout differs: 3 desk columns on desktop, 1 on phone, with drag as a desktop extra and ▲/▼ everywhere.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
The open Ask is always the lead, so it's one click (Extra!) away. Next unread: scan for bold, or step through the ticker. #7 is weak: it's a Full-edition In brief line on the Findings desk, so it takes Extra!, then Full, then a scan (about 3 clicks). The page has no jump-to-number.
At-150
The front page doesn't grow much: the lead and above the fold hold only Key and Balanced stories (about 20 at 150). In brief becomes long, and the page needs a "Continued on page 2" split. Recap cites and reply refs are unchanged, because #n is stable. The unread count stays on the Extra! line.
Build-cost
M to L. It needs the M2 strip, a layout engine for the edition, DnD with a touch fallback, and a headline field on each message: either the recap call writes headlines (+1 structured output) or Jev emits them. Storage: feedback.jsonl and categories.json, with a desk field added.
Trade-off
It's the most readable recap in the set and makes importance physical ("it belongs above the fold"). The costs are a big layout for a small number of messages, a thin front page at default weights (only the Ask and 3 decisions make the Late edition's upper half), a metaphor that fights live updates, and column inches that are just weight in costume. Steal: visited-link read state, meaning bold for unread and grey for read in any list of surfaced messages, and the fold as a drag target for a single, legible importance gesture.

Off the wall

W2 · Tier list

Jev's levels become an S/A/B/C tier list. Every pin wears its tier letter, the recap is read out one tier at a time, and you teach Jev by dragging a message tile to another row, or onto the composer to reply to it.

Builds on
B3's pin lane, clustering, loupe and slot, unchanged in behaviour. Each pin gets a tier letter above its number, the level control is relabelled as tier cut-offs (S · S–A · S–B · Final), and a second mode, ▦ Board, swaps nothing out but adds the tier list under the strip.
Placement
All inside the one activity card: pins over the strip, then a bar (Board, Tier recap, the ? #24 chip, the tier cut-off), then the recap and board when open, then the slot. The final reply and composer follow the card as today. Reply tokens land in the normal composer.
Live
New pins drop in at the right. The slot holds the open Ask #24, with ▲/▼ tier controls, Reply and a read sticker. "9 unread" sits in the head and every unread pin and tile carries a white dot. The composer shows the canonical draft with #24 and #18 tokens between text.
Settled
The desktop mockup opens with the tier recap and the board, so the whole turn is a 4-row list: S 6, A 10 (including #1 with ▲ you), B 18, C 0. The slot folds to a one-line peek of #24. "13 unread" is in the head.
Recap
"✦ Tier recap" on the bar, on request by default. sonnet-5 writes the canonical recap and conduit files each sentence under the tier of the message it cites, so it reads "S tier: one answer needed… A tier: … B tier: …". "Prose" shows the verbatim text. Settled adds a Whole turn scope, where #1's ▲ puts it in the A-tier sentence. Every [#n] is a button that selects the message, opens the slot and flashes its tile. Model, trigger, scope and length live in Settings › Recap.
Read-state
Leaving a message open for a second puts a silver sticker on it. Read tiles wear a sticker dot, and unread pins and tiles wear a white dot and a bold number. The slot's "Mark unread" button peels the sticker off. The head count updates live and is itself a button that jumps to the next unread.
Importance-feedback
Drag a tile to another row, or use ▲/▼ on the slot (one tier per press). The pin letter, the tile's row, the lane and the mark ("▲ you · Jev said B") all change together, and a reason row offers "changed the plan / user-visible / noise / already knew". Each move appends {"mark":"raise","from":"B","to":"A",…} to feedback.jsonl. It never changes a weight. Tier C means folded into the log.
Reply-to
↩ Reply on the slot inserts a .ref at the caret. On desktop you can also drag any tile out of the board and drop it between two words of the draft, and it lands at the drop point. × or Backspace removes a token. The agent gets the scenario's "Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): …" blocks in order.
Categories
Settings › Category tiers uses the same board: bands S 90–100, A 70–89, B 50–69 and C 1–49. Drag a category row into a band to set it to 100, 80, 60 or 40, or fine-tune with −/+ in steps of 5 (rows re-band as they cross a boundary). Retire drops a built-in into the Retired band with Restore. "+ Add category" appends a row with an inline editor, and custom rows get Edit and Delete.
Collapsible
▾ folds the slot to a peek line, and Board and Recap toggle off. With cut-off "Final" the lane disappears and the card is today's head plus strip. The head chevron opens the step log.
Short-session-threads
Default settled (board closed, slot folded): head, 2-line pin lane, strip, bar and peek, about 6 lines on desktop and 8 on phone. The board adds 4 rows (6 to 8 lines at 34, since tiles wrap). It is all one card.
Easy-to-read
The slot is B3's: full text at 13.5px with a large type label. Tier letters are greyscale (white S down to dark C), so they never compete with the type colours. The recap's tier letters give the gist order: read S, stop if busy.
Mobile-friendly
The same lane at 24px pins with GAP 28 clusters, the bar wraps to two rows, and tiles grow to 32px. All buttons are at least 32px. On phone you move tiles with the slot's ▲/▼, because a drag on a small board fights with scrolling. Tile drag still works there, but it isn't the taught path.
Consistency
Same lane, letters, board, sticker, recap and settings bands on both. Two differences: phone teaches ▲/▼ over drag, and on phone you reply with ↩ Reply rather than by dragging a tile to the composer, because the dock is below the fold of a tall board.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
#7 is a B-tier Finding. Pick S–B then its pin (2 clicks), or open Board and tap tile 7 (2), or type 7 Enter on the lane. The Ask: the ? #24 chip (1) or the a key, and it is always the first S tile. Next unread: tap the "9 unread" pill, or u. The lane also takes +/− (tier), r (reply) and b (board).
At-150
The lane clusters as B3 did, and the loupe spreads them. The board is where it strains: B holds about 110 tiles, so rows cap at two lines with "+84 more ›" (the tiles are drawn, the cap isn't). The recap still has one sentence per tier. The unread pill is a number, and tokens are unchanged.
Build-cost
M. It needs B3, a tier mapping over prominence (no new storage beyond read state and feedback.jsonl), one recap call per request plus a cheap sentence-to-tier split, and a pointer-drag layer for tiles and category rows.
Trade-off
Tiers are the same levels with a new vocabulary, and that is both the gain and the cost. "Drag to S" is instantly understood, but it hides the numeric prominence that makes levels predictable, and the board is a whole extra surface. Its drag-to-reply isn't discoverable, and the reorganised recap isn't the model's own sentence order. Steal: the recap sorted by importance tier (read the S line and stop), and one drag gesture that both reranks a message and teaches Jev.

Off the wall

W3 · Radio briefing

The recap is something you listen to: a spoken briefing with a karaoke transcript whose phrases are cited. The M2 strip's thumb is the playhead, so hearing the briefing walks you through the pins, and anything you've heard counts as read. Answer by holding the mic while a message plays.

Builds on
M2's two-row pin rail over the strip, its scrub-to-pin thumb and its floating card. The thumb now doubles as the playhead of a spoken briefing, and the card, now in the flow and tied to the thumb by its caret, shows whatever message is playing.
Placement
Inside the activity card: the head (with "9 unread"), then the player bar (play, title, level), the transcript when open, the pins and strip, and the card. The final reply and composer follow as today. Nothing plays by itself.
Live
The player reads "Briefing since 27:15 · 9 new · about 1:05". Pressing play reads the canonical live recap, then a rundown of the other six unread, one sentence each. New pins keep arriving at the right. The card holds Ask #24 with ▲/▼, "Hold to talk", "⌨ Reply" and "Mark heard". The composer carries the canonical two-ref draft.
Settled
The transcript is open by default: the canonical "While you were away" recap plus a rundown of the other eight unread (13 in all). The final reply sits below. Pin #1 carries "▲" and its card says "▲ you · Jev: All · changed the plan". Scope: Since I read or Whole turn.
Recap
The canonical sonnet-5 text, cut into phrases at its citations. The phrase being read fills left to right (karaoke). Every [#n] is a cite button that seeks the audio there, moves the thumb to the pin and opens the card. Clicking any phrase seeks to it. Speed is 1×, 1.5× or 2×. Voice is on-device TTS by default, so it costs nothing beyond the text recap ($0.005).
Read-state
Heard means read. A phrase's cited messages flip to read when it finishes, their pins lose the white dot with a small bump, the strip shades what you've heard, and the head count drops. The card's "Mark heard"/"Mark unheard" is the manual override. Unread messages below the current level still show as hollow dots on the strip, so the rundown's position is never invisible.
Importance-feedback
▲/▼ on the card, or ↑/↓ on the keyboard, apply to whatever is playing, without pausing. That lets you rate while listening: ▲ moves All→Balanced→Key, and ▼ moves Key→Balanced→All→Log (log removes the pin; the dot stays). Each mark appends to feedback.jsonl and never changes a station's weights.
Reply-to
Hold the mic (pointer or Space) while a message plays: the briefing ducks, you speak, and on release the message's token is inserted at the caret, followed by your words transcribed on-device. The typed fallback, ⌨ Reply, inserts the token for you to type after. × or Backspace removes a token. The agent gets the canonical "Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): …" blocks.
Categories
Settings › Stations. A preset is a named mix of category weights: 88.1 Balanced mix (the scenario defaults), 94.7 Blockers first, 101.3 Everything, and 106.5 Night shift. Tuning any fader turns it into "Custom mix", which "Save as station" keeps (custom stations can be deleted). Below that are per-category faders with −/+ (steps of 5), Retire/Restore for built-ins, and "+ Add category" with Edit/Delete for customs, ⚡ Perf included.
Collapsible
The transcript toggles open and closed, the card folds to a one-line peek, and the head chevron shows the step log. With level "Final" the rail hides and only the player and strip remain.
Short-session-threads
Collapsed it is the head, a 44px player bar, a 2-row rail and the strip, about 5 lines. That is heavier than B3 for a 3-message turn, because the player bar is always there. A turn with fewer than 3 unread shows no player bar, just M2's rail.
Easy-to-read
The transcript is ordinary prose at 13px and readable without sound. The karaoke highlight is a faint fill, not a colour change. The card is M2's, at 13.5px.
Mobile-friendly
This is the natural phone case: walking, listening, holding the mic. The play button is 40px, the pins have 32px tap halos, the mic is a 32px press-and-hold, and the card is full width. Playback continues with the screen locked through the Media Session API, which the mockup can't show.
Consistency
Same rail, strip-as-playhead, card, transcript and settings on both. Phone adds lock-screen transport controls, and the mic is the primary reply there.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
#7 is below Balanced. Choose All, then tap its pin (2 taps), or scrub the thumb until the card says #7 (1 drag). The Ask: its pulsing pin, the first transcript phrase, or a. The rail takes ←/→, Home/End, a, Space (play or pause) and ↑/↓ (rate). There's no find-by-number in audio.
At-150
The rail thins to dots as M2 did. The briefing covers only since-last-read, with the rundown capped at 8 ("and 23 more findings, all green") so audio stays under about 90s. Tokens are unchanged.
Build-cost
M-L. It needs M2, one text recap call, on-device TTS (Web Speech) with phrase boundary events for karaoke, MediaSession for the lock screen, and on-device speech-to-text for the mic, with a server STT fallback. There is no new storage beyond read state.
Trade-off
Audio is slow: 1:05 to hear what you can skim in 10s, and a meeting-heavy office or open plan makes it unusable. The payoff is real on a phone away from a keyboard. Hold-to-talk puts the token in without looking, but voice replies to a coding agent need an edit pass. Steal: "heard/read" as a side effect of consuming the recap, and a rundown that walks the thumb through every unread pin in order.

Off the wall

W4 · Metro map

The turn is a metro line and the surfaced messages are its stations. Decisions and replans are interchanges, with a dashed spur for the branch not taken. A pink "You are here" marks how far you've read, and unread stations are hollow. The recap reads as route directions.

Builds on
B3's idea of a lane of markers placed by time over the strip, redrawn as a transit diagram. The line is placed by time, and each track segment takes the colour of the station it leads to, so the whole route reads "Finding line to #1, Scope line to #3…". The pin lane is gone. "Lines" switches to a full map with one track per category, which the route snakes between.
Placement
Inside the activity card, under the head: the map (about 60px), then a bar (Lines, Route recap, the ? #24 chip, Next stop, level), then the recap and the station sign when open. The final reply and composer follow as today.
Live
The line ends in a dotted run to a blinking train at the live edge, labelled "running pnpm acceptance:visual". The pink "You are here" sits on #21, and #22–#30 are hollow (9 unread, in the head). The station sign for ? #24 is open with ▲ Enlarge, ▼ Shrink, "Message the driver" and "Read to here". The composer carries the canonical two-ref draft.
Settled
The line runs to a terminus at #34, and "13 unread" is in the head. The route recap is open with the since-you-read directions. Station #1 is drawn a size up with a ▲ badge ("▲ you"), one tap from its sign. Spurs show the branches not taken at #6, #9, #11, #18, #25, #32 and #33.
Recap
sonnet-5 writes the canonical recap, and conduit renders it as a route: one stop per cited message, in order. Each stop says which line you ride and where you change, with the canonical wording kept as each stop's text: "Change at ? #24 Ask: recapture phone-sidebar or keep the old paint order". Scope is Since I read or Whole turn (settled), and "Prose" shows the verbatim canonical paragraph. Every [#n] is a cite that opens the station sign and rings the station on the map.
Read-state
The read position is one marker. "You are here" sits on the last read station, and stations after it are hollow with bold numbers. "Next stop" or n moves you forward one station and fills it in. "Read to here" or "Unread from here" on a sign moves the marker directly. The count updates live. Marking one out-of-order message as read is not possible, by design.
Importance-feedback
Enlarge (▲) and Shrink (▼) on the sign change a station's size, which is its level: Key is the big roundel, Balanced medium, All small, and Log removes it from the map. The mark reads "▲ you · Jev: All". Each press logs to feedback.jsonl and never changes a line's weight.
Reply-to
Tap a station, then "Message the driver": the station's token goes into the composer at the caret. Repeat it for #18, typing in between. × or Backspace removes a token. The agent receives the canonical "Re #24 (Ask, 31:02): …" blocks.
Categories
Settings › Lines: every category is a line with a colour swatch, weight (−/+ by 5), definition and counts, drawn as a mini track. Built-ins can be retired (dashed line in a Retired section) and restored. "+ Add line" appends a custom line with an editor (name, glyph, definition, colour from 8 swatches). Custom lines, ⚡ Perf included, get Edit and Delete.
Collapsible
The sign and the recap close with ×. At level "Final" the map collapses to a 6px line with just the "You are here" dot and the Ask roundel. The head chevron shows the step log.
Short-session-threads
A 3-message turn is a short line with 3 stations and no bar clutter, about 3 lines under the head. That's lighter than the pin lanes, because the stations and the strip are one drawing.
Easy-to-read
The sign is plain 13.5px text under a platform-style header. The map is glanceable (big roundels are what mattered, pink is where you are) but it is not text, so it needs the sign or the recap to be read. The full Lines map is dense at 34 and more a novelty than a reading surface.
Mobile-friendly
The same line at phone width, with 32px invisible tap targets on every station, 32px buttons, and the sign full width. Labels at Balanced crowd between 01:42 and 04:05, so numbers step to a second row.
Consistency
Same map, sign, recap and settings on both. Phone hides the legend and uses 12px labels.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
#7 is a small All-level station. Pick All, then tap station 7 (2 taps). The station buttons are also in reading order for Tab, and ←/→ on the map moves between them. The Ask: its pulsing roundel, the ? #24 chip, or a. Next unread: Next stop, or n.
At-150
It strains here. At All, 150 stations in 560px is a comb, and the Lines map becomes unreadable. It holds up at Key (about 25 roundels) and Balanced, and the recap keeps to since-you-read. Station numbers thin to Key only above 40 stations. Tokens are unchanged.
Build-cost
M. An SVG renderer with a label-collision pass, a single read-position cursor (simpler than per-message read state), and the recap rendered from citations into stops. The branch-not-taken text needs one more field in Jev's output ("alternative": short phrase) for decisions and replans, and that costs tokens on every classification.
Trade-off
The metaphor is memorable and "You are here" is the clearest read-state in the set. But a single read cursor can't express "read #30 but not #26", branch-not-taken needs extra model output, and the Lines map is decoration past about 20 stations. Steal: the one-cursor "You are here" read position with Next stop, and showing decisions with the alternative they rejected.

Off the wall

W5 · Swipe deck

The slot under the pin lane is the top card of a deck: flick it right if it mattered more than Jev thought, left if less, up if the type is right, down to retype it, and hold it to reply, while a running "you vs Jev" score and the ledger it writes make every read a training signal.

Builds on
B3. Its pin lane, clustering, loupe and drag-scrub are kept as they were. B3's slot becomes the top card of a deck, with two card edges showing beneath it. The pins still pick which card is on top. What's new is that the card itself takes gestures.
Placement
Everything sits inside the one activity block: head (with the unread count), pin lane, strip, deck bar, deck, and one ledger line. The final reply follows the block, then the composer. Reply tokens land in that composer. The recap is a card in the deck, not a separate panel.
Live
The deck is dealt in this order: the recap card, then the open Ask, then the other unread cards in time order, then the read ones. The Live mockup has the recap card put away and #24 on top. New messages join the unread part of the deck, and each new pin drops in at the right end of the strip.
Settled
The deck reopens on the recap card ("since you last read", 13 updates), with a scope switch for the whole-turn recap. Flicking it away deals #24.
Recap
The recap is the first card of the deck and comes back with "✦ Recap" in the deck bar. Every [#n] is a .cite button: it brings that message's card to the top, highlights its pin, and marks it read. The model, when it runs, scope and length are set in Settings (default sonnet-5, on request). In this design "on request" means dealing the deck while there are unread messages. The footer shows the model, the update count, the time and the cost.
Read-state
A card becomes read when you swipe it, act on it, or bring it to the top yourself (a pin, a citation, ‹ ›, Next unread). The card the deck happens to open on stays unread until you touch it, so the Live frame still shows #24 as unread. "○ Mark unread" (key u) puts it back. Unread cards carry an "unread" tag and their pins a white dot. The head shows the count ("9 unread").
Importance-feedback
Flick right (→, or "▲ More") to raise a card one level. Flick left (←) to lower it. Flick up (↑) to agree with Jev's type. Flick down (↓) to retype it from a picker. Swipes apply the change and deal the next card. Buttons apply it and leave the card where it is. The card shows "▲ you · Jev said All → now Balanced", the pin gains ▲, and the level counts in the bar change. Each mark or retype is appended to feedback.jsonl (the ledger line under the deck shows the exact line). Agreement swipes only feed the "you vs Jev" score (98 of 121 = 81%). Settings turns the ledger into a suggested weight per category, with a preview on this turn, which you apply yourself. No weight ever changes automatically.
Reply-to
Hold a card for about half a second (or press ↩ Reply, or r). A .ref token is inserted at the composer's last caret position and the caret is placed after it, so you type straight on. Hold another card and type again, or click into the text first to put the token somewhere else. × or Backspace removes a token. "what the agent gets" previews the send: each token becomes a Re #n (Type, time): "quote…" header, followed by the text you typed after it.
Categories
Settings › Surfacing shows a table of the 9 built-ins plus ⚡ Perf: definition, a weight stepper, "your swipes" (▲/▼ this week, and a suggested weight you can use), and Retire. Retired built-ins move to a Retired section with Restore. Custom categories get Edit and Delete. "+ New category" appends a row. Above the table, a preview panel spells out what the suggestions would change on this turn.
Collapsible
▾ on the card folds the deck to a single peek line, with the edges shrunk. The pin lane stays, because it is the activity strip. Tap a pin or the peek to reopen. At the Final level (in Settings) the lane and deck are hidden, which is today's view.
Short-session-threads
Desktop, settled: head, lane, strip and axis (3 lines), the deck bar (1), the card (about 7 to 9) and the ledger line: about 13 lines, and 5 folded. Phone: about 17, because the six action buttons form a 3×2 grid. It is always one activity block, and the deck shows one card whatever the count.
Easy-to-read
One message at a time at 13.5px, never clamped, with a big type label, #24 · 31:02, and the level with its prominence ("Key · 97"). The swipe stamp (▲ MORE, ▼ LESS, ✓ RIGHT TYPE, ↻ RETYPE) names the action before you let go. The weak point is the action row: six buttons under every card is a lot of chrome.
Mobile-friendly
This is where the design is at home: thumb flicks, a 3×2 grid of 34px buttons, 24px pins, and the B3 loupe on dense stretches. The card sets touch-action:none, so vertical flicks don't scroll the page. You scroll from outside the card, which people have to learn.
Consistency
The card, stamps, actions, deck order, recap card and tokens are identical on both. Divergences: desktop maps the swipes to arrow keys and shows key hints, while the phone drops the hints and arranges the actions as a grid. The phone's deck bar wraps to two rows. Hold-to-reply exists on both (mouse press-and-hold works), and the ↩ button is always shown, because a hold can't be discovered.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
The open Ask: one tap ("? #24" in the bar) or a. It is also second in the deck. Next unread: one tap ("Next unread ⇥") or n. #7: at All, tap its pin or group and loupe (2 taps). On desktop, type 7 ↵, which switches to All if needed.
At-150
The lane turns into group pills, as in B3, and the loupe does the work. The deck still shows one card, and its position reads "1 / 150". Triaging 150 cards one at a time is where the concept strains. The recap card and "Next unread" are the escape hatches. The unread count stays a single number, and the tokens are unaffected. The agreement score gets more reliable the more you swipe.
Build-cost
M–L: B3's lane, plus gesture handling (drag, fling thresholds, long-press), the deck ordering, per-message read state and marks (a small store per session), feedback.jsonl appends, a recap call (about $0.006), and the suggestion maths in Settings. No new surface outside the block.
Trade-off
A reading surface that doubles as training turns every glance into a judgement, and after a week that becomes a chore. Flicks are also easy to fire by accident (the ledger line, and flicking again, undo them). One card at a time can't show two messages side by side. Steal: the "you vs Jev" agreement score, and weight suggestions computed from the ledger with a preview on the current turn. Together they make the feedback loop visible and safe without the deck.

Off the wall

W6 · Plain-text journal

Every surfaced message is appended to .conduit/journal/<session>.md and read in a less-style pager inside the activity block, where the recap is a generated ## Recap section, importance is a +1 reason line you add, reply is > #24, and categories are a surfacing.toml you edit with a live diff.

Builds on
Nothing in B1–B7 or M1–M7. It borrows the pager from less and the journal from plain-text note tools. The only visual primitives it reuses are the shell's activity block, strip, .ref and .cite.
Placement
The one activity block contains the head (with the unread count and a "less"/"tail" toggle), a row of type-coloured ticks over the strip, and either a three-line tail of the journal (closed) or the pager (open). The pager has a filename bar, level filter, line-numbered view, inverse status line, command line and key row. The final reply and the composer come after it. The journal file itself is real: <project>/.conduit/journal/ses_c2d8cd52.md.
Live
Each newly surfaced message appends an entry, and the pager keeps its place, as less +F would if you had scrolled up. The status line shows the file position and "9 unread". The Live mockup has the pager open with the cursor on #24, which is also marked "waiting on you".
Settled
Conduit writes (or rewrites) a ## Recap section at the end of the file, and the pager opens at it. g goes back to the top, where #1 is.
Recap
The recap is a generated markdown section with [#n] links. Each link is a .cite that moves the cursor to that entry and marks it read. R, or :recap, (re)generates it: "since you last read" by default, :recap turn for the whole turn (settled only), which you can also switch from the header comment. A comment line records the model, update count, time and cost. It follows [recap] in surfacing.toml (sonnet-5, on request).
Read-state
Each heading holds a checkbox: ## [ ] #24 is unread, [x] is read. The box is in the file, so the file is the read state. An unread entry also gets a ● in the gutter and a white tick above the strip. Moving the cursor onto an entry (j/k, u, a click, a citation) ticks it. m, or clicking the box, toggles it. The head badge and status line keep the count.
Importance-feedback
+ prompts for "+1 reason" and appends a line such as +1 changed the plan under the entry. - appends -1 reason. The heading's level then reads All → Balanced. The same mark is appended to feedback.jsonl (the status line confirms this). Pressing the opposite key removes the annotation. A −1 at All folds the entry into the log, so it disappears at every level filter. Because the annotations are plain lines, you can also type them into the file by hand, and conduit picks them up.
Reply-to
r quotes the entry under the cursor into the composer as a > #24 Ask token, placed at the composer's last caret position, with the caret after it. Repeat for several entries and type between them. × or Backspace removes a token. "Preview send" shows the expanded Re #n (Type, time): "…" blocks the agent receives.
Categories
Categories are the [categories] and [custom] tables of ~/.config/conduit/surfacing.toml, as multi-line inline tables (TOML 1.1). The in-app editor has − / + on each weight, retire (which moves the entry into [retired], where restore is), and + add, edit and delete for custom entries. A diff pane shows every unsaved change against the saved file, with :w to write and :e! to revert. [recap] and [feedback] live in the same file.
Collapsible
q (or "tail" in the head) closes the pager to a three-line tail -n 3 of the journal, and "less" reopens it at the same place. The level filter (& in less terms: key, balanced, all) hides entries below it, and hidden line numbers stay skipped, as in less.
Short-session-threads
Closed, the block is head, ticks and strip, and 3 tail lines: about 5 lines. Open, the pager is a fixed 20 rows on desktop (18 on phone) whatever the message count. It is always one block.
Easy-to-read
Each entry is a bold heading (## [ ] #24 · 31:02 · ? Ask · p.97 · Key) followed by the unclamped message, with a blank line between entries. Line numbers and markdown sigils add noise, and the type colour is confined to the glyph and label. People who live in terminals will read it faster than cards. Everyone else will find it dense. That is the concept's honest cost.
Mobile-friendly
A Termux-style extra-keys block (two rows of seven 40px keys: j k u a g G R and / + − m r : q) stands in for the keyboard. The whole heading can be tapped to move the cursor. The level filter and checkboxes have enlarged hit areas, and the command line opens the soft keyboard only for reasons, search and :. It works, but it is a desktop idiom carried to the phone.
Consistency
The file, entries, keys, commands and tokens are identical on both. The only divergence is the key row: desktop shows inline key hints, the phone a 7×2 key grid.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
The open Ask: a, or one tap. Next unread: u, or one tap. #7: :7 ↵ (it switches the filter to all if needed), or /push-routing ↵. On the phone that is 2 taps plus typing. Top and bottom: g and G.
At-150
At 150 entries the file is about 450 lines, which a pager handles easily. The status line reads "lines 212–231/468 45%", search and :n scale, and the level filter keeps Balanced at around 60 entries. The ticks over the strip merge into a texture, and that is acceptable because they are decorative. Unread tracking stays exact because it lives in the checkboxes.
Build-cost
M: a journal writer in the daemon (append-only, plus in-place checkbox and annotation edits), a pager component (virtualised lines, key map, command line), a TOML parser and serialiser with a line diff, and the recap call. A file watcher lets hand edits flow back. It needs no new visual primitives.
Trade-off
It is the most portable and scriptable design here. You can grep, commit and hand the file to another agent. But it asks everyone to read in a terminal idiom, and read state stored in a markdown file will run into concurrent writes, for example the agent appending while you tick a box. Steal: write surfaced messages to a plain journal file anyway, even with a different UI. The +1 reason line is the most honest feedback format, because it is readable, editable, and already the training data.

Off the wall

W7 · Quest log

The turn is a quest: a small tracker on the activity block shows the main quest, the one entry awaiting your answer and the active objective, and "Quest log" opens an RPG-style journal (objectives, side quests, lore, and a Chronicle recap) where you rate entries with stars, see "new" sparkles and pick "Respond" to quote an entry into your reply.

Builds on
M2's settled strip (a plain strip, with no pins) and the shell's activity block. The idea of a quest tracker plus a journal comes from RPG HUDs. The quest log itself is new: none of B1–B7, M1–M7 or W1–W6 group messages by what they mean to the job (objective, obstacle, lore).
Placement
The activity block holds the shell head, the strip, and then either the tracker or the quest log. The tracker is 4 rows: the main quest with its progress, the glowing "Awaiting your answer" entry, the active objective, and "Quest log" and "Chronicle" buttons. The quest log opens inside the same block. On desktop it is two panes (the log on the left, a dialogue box on the right). On the phone it is one pane that switches between the log and the dialogue. The final reply and the composer come after the block.
Live
Each new message takes its place in the log by kind: a Milestone is a completed objective, a Risk, Blocked or Scope entry is a side quest, an Ask becomes "Awaiting your answer", and everything else is lore. New entries sparkle ✦. The active objective reads the agent's current step ("running pnpm acceptance:visual"). The Live mockups have the log open on #24.
Settled
The tracker's progress bar reads 7 of 8, and the one gap is the awaiting answer. The active objective becomes "Turn complete · branch pushed". Desktop opens the log on the Chronicle. The phone keeps the 4-row tracker, and the Chronicle is one tap away.
Recap
The Chronicle is the first entry in the log, and it is the recap: narrated text in the dialogue box, where every [#n] is a .cite that opens that entry and marks it read. You can switch it between since last read and the whole turn. The footer shows the model and cost, with "↻ Rewrite". In Live it is written on request ("Write the chronicle"), following Settings › Chronicler.
Read-state
Unread entries carry a ✦ sparkle in the log and "✦ new" in the dialogue box. Opening an entry, whether by clicking, j/k, "Next new" or a citation, marks it read. Dialogue option 2 ("Mark as new") reverses that. The count sits on the tracker's Quest log button ("✦ 9 new") and in the open log's header. The initial selection in each mockup is left unread on purpose, so the marker shows.
Importance-feedback
Importance is a 3-star rating: ★ All, ★★ Balanced, ★★★ Key, plus "✕ hide", which sends the entry to the log. Jev's rating shows as hollow outline stars next to your filled ones. Picking Jev's own level clears your rating. When your rating differs, the row shows a "you" tag, a "why?" field appears, and feedback.jsonl records a raise or lower with from, to and the reason. #1 shows Jev ★, you ★★, "changed the plan". Ratings apply live, so the entry moves in or out of the star filter.
Reply-to
Dialogue option 1, "Respond…" (or 1 / r), inserts a ↩ #24 Ask .ref token at the composer's last caret position. You can add several and type between them. × or Backspace removes a token. "Preview send" shows the Re #n (Type, time): "…" blocks the agent receives.
Categories
Settings › Quest types lists each type with its glyph, label, colour, quest kind (Awaiting, Objective, Side quest, Lore) and an XP weight (± 5). XP × Jev's confidence decides the stars (70 for ★★★, 40 for ★★). Built-ins can be retired to "Retired quest types", restored from there, and reset. Custom types (⚡ Perf) can be edited and deleted, and "+ New quest type" adds one, including its kind.
Collapsible
× (or Esc) closes the log to the 4-row tracker. The tracker never grows. Within the log, each section (Objectives, Side quests, Lore) folds on its header, and the star filter (★★★ / ★★+ / ★+) trims Side quests and Lore. The main quest and the awaiting entry are always shown.
Short-session-threads
The collapsed block is the head, the strip and 4 tracker rows, about 150px at any message count. The open log is a fixed 430px panel that scrolls inside. It is always one block.
Easy-to-read
The log is grouped by what an entry means to the job, which is easier to scan than a timeline. Each dialogue box is one message at 13.5px, with its type glyph and label in colour and the stars next to it. Gold and serif stay on headings, so the game framing doesn't touch the text itself. The risk is that some readers will find the framing twee.
Mobile-friendly
The log and the dialogue are pages in the same panel: tap a row to open its dialogue, and "‹ Quest log" goes back. Rows are 44px, options and stars 36–40px, and the tracker's awaiting row is a 44px glowing target. The phone has no hotkey row, because the numbered options are the touch path.
Consistency
The tracker, log sections, dialogue options, stars and tokens are the same on desktop and phone. There are two divergences: desktop shows log and dialogue side by side where the phone pages between them, and the keyboard hints (j/k/u/a/1–4/Esc) are desktop-only.
Dev-Navigation-Ease-And-Speed
The open Ask is one tap, on the glowing tracker row, whether the log is open or closed. Next unread is "Next new ✦" (u). #7 is under Lore, with ★ on: 2 taps, or j through the list. The log has no search or jump-to-number, so reaching an arbitrary number is slower than in W6.
At-150
The sections grow, but the panel stays at 430px and scrolls. At ★★+, Lore holds about 30 entries and Side quests about 12. Objectives fold by default above 8. The tracker is unchanged. Grouping by kind loses the chronology, which the times and #n on every row partly restore. With several Asks, "Awaiting your answer" becomes a short stack and the tracker shows the oldest.
Build-cost
M: the kind mapping (per type, set in settings), the side-quest "cleared by #n" links (these need the classifier to link a later message to an earlier one, which Jev doesn't do today, so the mock hard-codes them), the log and dialogue components, star ratings over the existing mark ledger, and the recap call. The active objective comes from the current step.
Trade-off
Grouping by meaning (what's done, what's in the way, what's waiting on you) is the best "where are we" view in the set, and the tracker is a small, glanceable summary. But the RPG framing will split the audience, and "cleared by" needs link inference Jev doesn't do yet. Steal: the 4-row tracker (main task · progress · the one thing awaiting you · the active step) as the collapsed state of any design, and stars as a clearer name for the three levels than Key, Balanced and All.
